arxiv-1707-08204.title: Power Control for Multi-Cell Networks with Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access Z. Yang, W. Xu, Y. Pan and M. Chen are with the National Mobile Communications Research Laboratory, Southeast University, Nanjing 211111, China, Email: {yangzhaohui, wxu, panyijin, chenming}@seu.edu.cn. C. Pan and M. Elkashlan
arxiv-1707-08204.creator: Zhaohui Yang, Cunhua Pan, , Wei Xu, , Yijin Pan, Ming Chen, , and Maged Elkashlan
arxiv-1707-08204.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Zhaohui Yang, Cunhua Pan, , Wei Xu, , Yijin Pan, Ming Chen, , and Maged Elkashlan. In this paper, we investigate the problems of sum power minimization and sum rate maximization for multi-cell networks with non-orthogonal multiple access. Considering the sum power minimization, we obtain closed-form solutions to the optimal power allocation strategy and then successfully transform the original problem to a linear one with a much smaller size, which can be optimally solved by using the standard interference function.

arxiv-2203-07164.title: Inverse moving point source problem for the wave equation
arxiv-2203-07164.creator: Hanin Al Jebawy , Abdellatif El Badia and Faouzi Triki
arxiv-2203-07164.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the problem of identifying a single moving point source for a three-dimensional wave equation from boundary measurements. Precisely, we show that the knowledge of the field generated by the source at six different points of the boundary over a finite time interval is sufficient to determine uniquely its trajectory.

arxiv-2209-04376.title: Challenges of Implementing Agile Processes in Remote-First Companies
arxiv-2209-04376.creator: Lulit Asfaw 1 , Mikael Clemmons 1 , Cody Hayes 1 , Elise Letnaunchyn 1 , Elnaz Rabieinejad 2
arxiv-2209-04376.description: Abstract The trend of remote work, especially in the IT sector, has been on the rise in recent years, and its popularity has especially increased since the COVID-19 pandemic. In addition to adopting remote work, companies also have been migrating toward managing their projects using agile processes. Agile processes promote small and continuous feedback loops powered by effective communication.

arxiv-2507-15032.title: The hunt for new pulsating ultraluminous X-ray sources: a clustering approach
arxiv-2507-15032.creator: N. O. Pinciroli Vago, R. Amato ⋆, M. Imbrogno, G. L. Israel, A. Belfiore, K. Kovlakas, P. Fraternali, M. Pasquato
arxiv-2507-15032.description: Abstract Context. The discovery of fast and variable coherent signals in a handful of ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) testifies to the presence of super-Eddington accreting neutron stars, and drastically changed the understanding of the ULX class. Our capability of discovering pulsations in ULXs is limited, among others, by poor statistics.

britannica-1911-thegn.title: Thegn (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-thegn.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-thegn.description: Article 'Thegn' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 26), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. The increase in the number of thegns produced in time a subdivision of the order. There arose a class of king’s thegns, corresponding to the earlier thegns, and a larger class of inferior thegns, some of them the thegns of bishops or of other thegns. A king’s thegn was a person of great importance, the contemporary idea being shown by the Latin translation of the words as comes.

pmc-11372486.title: Factors associated with thirty-day mortality and intensive care unit admission in patients undergoing hip fracture surgery
pmc-11372486.creator: Elvan Tekir Yılmaz, Yiğit Şahin, Bilge Olgun Keleş, Ali Altınbaş
pmc-11372486.description: BACKGROUND:Various factors contribute to the development of mortality and morbidity in hip fracture surgeries. This study aims to investigate the effects of modifiable factors such as the type of anesthesia, anesthesia management, surgical method, and timing of surgery on 30-day mortality rates, intensive care unit admissions, and complications.

pmc-12662573.title: The effects of lifestyle improvements and mindfulness-based stress reduction on pregnancy rate and anxiety in infertile women undergoing IVF: A randomized clinical trial
pmc-12662573.creator: Padideh Malekpour, Zahra Motaghi, Robab Hasanzadeh, Reza Chaman, Farjamfar Maryam, Mojgan Javedani Masroor
pmc-12662573.description: BACKGROUND:The lengthy and multi-stage nature of assisted reproductive technology (ART) can impose financial and social burdens on couples while also affecting their psychological well-being. Mindfulness-based stress reduction techniques help individuals cope effectively and cultivate inner calm. Additionally, lifestyle choices can impact fertility outcomes.

pmc-12849257.title: The eye–mind connection: a systematic review of retinal biomarkers and ocular signatures in major psychiatric disorders
pmc-12849257.creator: Raha Motamedi, Fatemeh Hayeri Mehrizi, Mohaddeseh Zeinali Ali Abadi, Mohamadreza Mohagheghi, Fatemeh Nourollahi Fomeshi, Seyyede Elahe Mousavikhah, Anis Ghaffarzadeh, Shayan Yaghmayee, Melika Arab Bafrani, Seyyed Kiarash Sadat Rafiei, Daniel Shafiei, Mahsa Asadi Anar, Farbod khosravi, Sanam Faizabad
pmc-12849257.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPsychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depression, and dementia are increasingly associated with specific ocular and retinal abnormalities. These associations may reflect shared neurovascular, inflammatory, and neurodegenerative mechanisms, yet findings remain scattered and understudied. This systematic review synthesizes existing evidence on ocular and retinal pathologies across major psychiatric conditions, highlighting common retinal biomarkers that may inform future screening strategies.MethodsFollowing PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase was conducted.

pmc-13023199.title: From diverse CT scans to generalization: towards robust abdominal organ segmentation
pmc-13023199.creator: Nicolás Álvarez Llopis, Felipe Ocampo Osorio, Jesús Alejandro Álzate-Grisales, Alejandro Mora Rubio, Francisco García García, Reinel Tabares-Soto, María de la Iglesia Vaya
pmc-13023199.description: Abdominal organ segmentation is a rapidly advancing area in medical imaging, boasting numerous remarkable applications in clinical and research settings. Despite these advancements, most existing segmentation models are developed using single-source data. This homogeneity raises concerns regarding the applicability of these models to more diverse and complex clinical scenarios.

pmc-13136653.title: Atypical Presentation of Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma as a Fever of Unknown Origin Mimicking Multiple Liver Abscesses: A Case Report
pmc-13136653.creator: Yuvrajsing K Pakal, Neha P Dharap, Shreya N Gade
pmc-13136653.description: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma typically presents late, most often with nonspecific symptoms such as weight loss, jaundice, and abdominal pain. Presentation with prolonged fever and weakness mimicking an infectious etiology is exceedingly rare. We report a case of a 54-year-old man with no known comorbidities who presented with persistent fever, cough, and weakness of 20 days' duration.

pmc-13436311.title: The impacts of peace and conflict resolution interventions on mental health and psychological well-being: a systematic review
pmc-13436311.creator: María Camila García Durán, Rakesh Singh, Mauricio Avendano, Crick Lund
pmc-13436311.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPrior studies have examined the impact of armed conflict on mental health. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on how peace and conflict resolution interventions influence the mental health and well-being of conflict-affected communities.MethodsWe conducted a systematic review across multiple databases and identified studies evaluating the effects of peace and conflict resolution interventions on mental health and well-being from 1990 to 2026.
